item.title: Book Review: The Unfinished Harauld Hughes - Richard Ayoade ★★★⯪☆
item.description: A decade ago, I read Ayoade's first book. In my review, I said: It's hard to know how to assess a book like this. item.title: Some thoughts on restaurant menu QR codes
item.description: Is anyone else SICK AND TIRED of the way hotels now foist plastic "keycards" on guests? No! I don't want tap to open my door! No! I don't want to keep the card in my wallet! No! I don't want electronics in control of my life! What if I need to stab an attacker? item.title: Book Review: When the Dust Settles - Stories of Love, Loss and Hope from an Expert in Disaster by Lucy Easthope ★★★★★
item.description: This is a difficult but essential book. I was initially put off by how graphically autobiographical it is. The disaster planning I came for was frequently interrupted with the author's loves, disasters, health issues, pains, and domestic issues. As the book wore on, I realised how vital that is. Disasters - whether natural or caused by human actions - cannot be tackled in a dispassionate way.…

item.title: Book Review: The God of Small Things by Arundhati Roy ★★☆☆☆
item.description: I did not care for this one bit. I found it cloying, infantilising, and far too circuitous. It starts off as a bit of an overwritten melodrama, where every phrase is a delicious flower waiting to bloom, but ends up being a over-sugared mess with a rotten heart. Parts are just exhausting to read, with no time to catch your breath between scenes. That can work in some books when spaced out -…
